requirements.requirement: Treat /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 as the source of truth and keep node2 synchronized from it.
requirements.summary: Node2 was configured to pull only node1's file through a restricted export command and atomically replace its local copy. The initial synchronization succeeded, and the final files had identical SHA-256 hashes after both restarts.

requirements.requirement: Pick up any node1 configuration change on node2 within 15 minutes.
requirements.summary: A timestamped change made on node1 at 09:56:04 was automatically present on node2 with the same hash by 09:56:45, approximately 41 seconds later. The probe was then removed and the clean state resynchronized.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct transition evidence demonstrates automatic propagation well inside 15 minutes, cleanup and resynchronization, matching final state, and persistence after restarting both nodes. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service and data state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree with the executor's restart observations.
limitations: The propagation timing was demonstrated with one induced change rather than repeated over a longer observation period; the recurring five-minute timer configuration and post-restart automatic run provide supporting evidence for continued operation.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the initially absent source file, restricted SSH export path, synchronization script, and persistent timer directly supported the task (cmd-c2919b94ac8c4411, cmd-8cf247dd39c34032, cmd-664119f2517a482a). The temporary synchronization probe was bounded and fully reverted (cmd-7272ca72f50f46c2, cmd-2669d4a9f3534430, cmd-e8c74b6f8b0e4c3c). Restarts were required evidence-protocol actions. Final snapshots show no failed services, new listening ports, or package damage.
